{"items":[{"doc_id":"c3457f70-372d-475e-80c3-18bfd4037194","seq":1,"headings":["Northstar Support Service Level Schedule v2.0","1. Application"],"text":"This version applies to tickets opened on or after 2026-04-01 00:00 CT. The version is chosen by the ticket's **open time in Central
Time**, and nothing else. A ticket keeps its version for its whole life, including credits, cap
and claim window, even if it is restored, claimed or decided after another version takes effect.
The UTC date of the open time, the restoration date and the claim date do not change the version."},{"doc_id":"c3457f70-372d-475e-80c3-18bfd4037194","seq":2,"headings":["Northstar Support Service Level Schedule v2.0","2. Definitions"],"text":"2.1 **Time zone.** All service-level times, business hours, deadlines and calendar dates are in US
Central Time (America/Chicago), written "CT". Central Standard Time is UTC−06:00 and Central
Daylight Time is UTC−05:00. CDT applied from 2025-03-09 to 2025-11-02, and from 2026-03-08. A
timestamp recorded in another zone (for example Eastern Daylight Time, UTC−04:00, or UTC in system
logs) is converted to CT before anything is measured. "Date" (the restoration date, the claim date
or a notice date) means the CT calendar date of the timestamp after conversion.

2.2 **Business hours** are 08:00 to 18:00 CT, Monday to Friday, except Northstar holidays (see the
Northstar holiday calendar). A business day is a Monday-to-Friday date that is not a Northstar
holiday. Every business day has exactly 10 business hours."},{"doc_id":"c3457f70-372d-475e-80c3-18bfd4037194","seq":3,"headings":["Northstar Support Service Level Schedule v2.0","2. Definitions"],"text":"2.3 **Clocks.** Every ticket has a response clock and a restoration clock, which start together. A
24×7 clock counts all elapsed time; across a daylight-saving change it counts the actual elapsed
time. A business-hours clock counts only time inside business hours. Elapsed time is measured in
whole minutes. Pauses apply only to the restoration clock; maintenance exclusions apply to both.

2.4 **Met or missed.** A target elapses at the moment its clock reaches the target duration. A
target is met if the event happens at or before that moment, and missed if it happens after it.
An event exactly at the moment the target elapses meets it.

2.5 **Open time.** Every support request is a ticket in Northstar Service (SR-nnnnn). Its open time
is the moment a hotline call is answered, a portal submission is received, or an email to
support@northstar.example is received. When an incident actually began (if earlier) is not the open
time and starts no clock."},{"doc_id":"c3457f70-372d-475e-80c3-18bfd4037194","seq":4,"headings":["Northstar Support Service Level Schedule v2.0","2. Definitions"],"text":"2.6 **Initial response** is the first communication to the customer, by telephone or as a ticket
comment, from a Northstar support engineer that addresses the specific issue. A request from an
engineer for information, access or an action counts. Automated acknowledgments, auto-replies and
ticket-creation notices do not count, and neither does a call made by the customer.

2.7 **Restoration** is the moment the affected product is returned to production use, as recorded
in Northstar Service, through a fix or through a workaround that removes the business impact on
which the severity was based. A later permanent fix is not measured. For a Severity 1 ticket, a
workaround that lets production or operations resume counts as restoration even if it needs ongoing

tied to the response on the response clock, deadlines tied to restoration on the restoration clock
(paused time does not count), and a qualifying maintenance window delays both. The customer-caused
exclusion and the telephone rule do not affect escalation. Each deadline is the latest compliant
time. "Engage" means assign the person to the ticket and confirm it there; "notify" means send a

   start.

   start.
3. If the ticket is not restored when 50% of the restoration target has elapsed, notify the
   **Director of Customer Support** no later than that moment.
4. If the ticket is not restored when 100% of the restoration target has elapsed, notify the
   **VP Sales** no later than that moment, and, for a **Strategic** account (CRM account tier), the
   **Chief Revenue Officer** as well."},{"doc_id":"2ec9d1dd-8f5b-4bb7-bd62-8d505a431c37","seq":3,"headings":["Support Escalation Procedure","Severity 2"],"text":"1. If there has been no initial response when the response target elapses, notify the **Support
   Escalation Manager** no later than that moment.

   Customer Support** and the **account owner** no later than that moment."},{"doc_id":"2ec9d1dd-8f5b-4bb7-bd62-8d505a431c37","seq":4,"headings":["Support Escalation Procedure","Severity 3 and 4"],"text":"On a Severity 3 ticket not restored when the restoration target elapses, notify the **Support
Escalation Manager** no later than that moment. Severity 4 has no escalation."},{"doc_id":"2ec9d1dd-8f5b-4bb7-bd62-8d505a431c37","seq":5,"headings":["Support Escalation Procedure","Tickets outside a support agreement"],"text":"A ticket is in scope only if its customer (identified by CRM account id, ERP customer id or DUNS,
never by name alone) has a support agreement covering the ticket's product, and the ticket was
opened on or after the coverage start. Out-of-scope tickets are handled best effort: severity is
classified only for internal priority, no targets apply (nothing can be breached and no credit is
owed), and the escalations above do not apply. Northstar Support must notify the **account owner**
of the ticket's CRM account no later than 10 business hours after the open time. Any credit claim
is declined, and the decision is sent as for any claim."},{"doc_id":"2ec9d1dd-8f5b-4bb7-bd62-8d505a431c37","seq":6,"headings":["Support Escalation Procedure","Root cause and claims"],"text":"When Northstar asserts the customer-caused exclusion, the **Support Engineering Lead** records the
root-cause finding by the deadline in the Service Level Schedule. For every credit claim, the
**Director of Customer Support** sends the written decision, and for an approved credit the
**Support Billing Manager** issues the credit memo, by the deadlines in the Service Level Schedule."},{"doc_id":"2ec9d1dd-8f5b-4bb7-bd62-8d505a431c37","seq":7,"headings":["Support Escalation Procedure","When a decision can't be made"],"text":"A determination can't be made when a fact it depends on is missing from the ticket record and no

description and notes). Test the definitions in order; the severity is the first one the recorded
impact meets."},{"doc_id":"b12e71cf-cafa-4cf8-b96a-1d05ed66fb5b","seq":2,"headings":["Support Severity Guide","Severity 1: Critical"],"text":"A Northstar product failure that, with **no workaround available**, either (a) stops the customer's
production or operations (a production line, a plant process, or a distribution, dispatch or
facility-operations activity cannot continue), or (b) makes NS-Cloud unavailable to **all** of the
customer's users."},{"doc_id":"b12e71cf-cafa-4cf8-b96a-1d05ed66fb5b","seq":3,"headings":["Support Severity Guide","Severity 2: High"],"text":"Not Severity 1, and any one of: (a) production or operations continue but are materially degraded;
(b) a control, alarming or condition-monitoring function is unavailable (not merely intermittent)
for one or more machines, lines, buildings or sites, whether or not the customer covers it with
manual checks; (c) NS-Cloud is unavailable to some, but not all, of the customer's users or sites;
(d) a Severity 1 condition with a workaround in place that needs ongoing manual effort."},{"doc_id":"b12e71cf-cafa-4cf8-b96a-1d05ed66fb5b","seq":4,"headings":["Support Severity Guide","Severity 3: Medium"],"text":"Not Severity 1 or 2: a function is impaired with no reduction in production output and no loss of a
control, alarming or monitoring function (intermittent faults with backfilled data, slow
performance, a failing report, a single-user error)."},{"doc_id":"b12e71cf-cafa-4cf8-b96a-1d05ed66fb5b","seq":5,"headings":["Support Severity Guide","Severity 4: Low"],"text":"A question, how-to, documentation issue, cosmetic defect or enhancement request, with no effect on
operations."},{"doc_id":"b12e71cf-cafa-4cf8-b96a-1d05ed66fb5b","seq":6,"headings":["Support Severity Guide","Who decides"],"text":"The customer's reported priority (P1 to P4) is only the customer's view: it does not set the
severity and has no effect on targets, credits or escalations. Northstar may correct the severity
up or down at any time. If the impact recorded at opening meets a different severity, that severity
governs from the open time, with its clock, targets, credits and escalations. If the impact changes
after opening, the ticket is reclassified at the moment the change is recorded."}],"total":6}

impact meets."},{"doc_id":"b12e71cf-cafa-4cf8-b96a-1d05ed66fb5b","seq":2,"headings":["Support Severity Guide","Severity 1: Critical"],"text":"A Northstar product failure that, with **no workaround available**, either (a) stops the customer's
production or operations (a production line, a plant process, or a distribution, dispatch or
facility-operations activity cannot continue), or (b) makes NS-Cloud unavailable to **all** of the
customer's users."},{"doc_id":"b12e71cf-cafa-4cf8-b96a-1d05ed66fb5b","seq":3,"headings":["Support Severity Guide","Severity 2: High"],"text":"Not Severity 1, and any one of: (a) production or operations continue but are materially degraded;
(b) a control, alarming or condition-monitoring function is unavailable (not merely intermittent)
for one or more machines, lines, buildings or sites, whether or not the customer covers it with
manual checks; (c) NS-Cloud is unavailable to some, but not all, of the customer's users or sites;
(d) a Severity 1 condition with a workaround in place that needs ongoing manual effort."},{"doc_id":"b12e71cf-cafa-4cf8-b96a-1d05ed66fb5b","seq":4,"headings":["Support Severity Guide","Severity 3: Medium"],"text":"Not Severity 1 or 2: a function is impaired with no reduction in production output and no loss of a
control, alarming or monitoring function (intermittent faults with backfilled data, slow
performance, a failing report, a single-user error)."},{"doc_id":"b12e71cf-cafa-4cf8-b96a-1d05ed66fb5b","seq":5,"headings":["Support Severity Guide","Severity 4: Low"],"text":"A question, how-to, documentation issue, cosmetic defect or enhancement request, with no effect on
operations."},{"doc_id":"b12e71cf-cafa-4cf8-b96a-1d05ed66fb5b","seq":6,"headings":["Support Severity Guide","Who decides"],"text":"The customer's reported priority (P1 to P4) is only the customer's view: it does not set the
severity and has no effect on targets, credits or escalations. Northstar may correct the severity
up or down at any time. If the impact recorded at opening meets a different severity, that severity
governs from the open time, with its clock, targets, credits and escalations. If the impact changes
after opening, the ticket is reclassified at the moment the change is recorded."}],"total":6}

I have all the rules and records I need. I'm doing the clock arithmetic now and then writing up the decision.

**Decision: NO_BREACH. Ticket SR-39561 met both its targets, so no service credit is owed. The credit claim must be declined in writing.**

**1. The customer.** CRM-2051 is BlueRiver Logistics, DUNS 07-331-9025. The support terms (SUP-BRL-2025) name Blue River Logistics LLC under the same DUNS. That gives a Silver plan, covering NS-CLOUD, from 2025-01-01 00:00 CT, at $2,500 a month. The CRM account tier is Standard.

**2. Scope.** In scope. The product is NS-CLOUD and the ticket opened on 2026-07-11, after coverage started.

**3. True severity: Severity 1.** The ticket says NS-Cloud is down for all users, dispatch can't see any shipments, and there is no workaround. That meets the severity guide's Severity 1 tests (b), NS-Cloud unavailable to all users, and (a), dispatch stopped. The customer reported it as P1, but that doesn't set the severity.

**4. Schedule version.** The ticket opened 2026-07-11 at 23:20 CDT (UTC−05:00), which falls under Schedule v2.0 (it covers tickets opened from 2026-04-01). Severity 1 runs on a 24×7 clock, whatever the plan. The targets are a 30-minute initial response and 4-hour restoration.

**5. Clock start: scheduled maintenance applies.**
- Maintenance notice MN-2607 covers this account and NS-CLOUD. The window ran 2026-07-11 22:00 to 2026-07-12 02:00 CT.
- The notice was sent 2026-06-26. Counting business days after that date up to the window's start gives 9 (Jun 29–30, Jul 1–2 and Jul 6–10; Jul 3 is a Northstar holiday). That is more than the 5 required, so the window qualifies.
- The ticket opened inside the window, so both clocks start when the window ends: **2026-07-12 02:00 CT**.
- No pauses were recorded and no customer-caused exclusion was asserted.
- The engineer's note says the upgrade in MN-2607 caused the outage. That doesn't change anything: time after the window counts normally, and time inside it doesn't count.

**6. Measurement.**
- **Response: met.** The engineer phoned at 23:35, before the clock started, so it counts as elapsed time zero.
- **Restoration: met.** Service was restored 2026-07-12 at 05:05. That is 3 hours 5 minutes on the clock, within the 4-hour target.

**7. Credits: $0.** BlueRiver's claim, received 2026-07-14 by email, was on time (the claim window ran to 2026-08-11 23:59 CT). It asks for a credit for "5 h 45 min", which counts from the open time and includes the excluded maintenance window. No target was missed, so nothing is owed.

**8. What Northstar owes.** Escalation deadlines run on the ticket's clocks, which the maintenance window delays:
- **Engage Hannah Lindqvist** (Support Escalation Manager) as incident lead by 2026-07-12 02:15 CT.
- **Notify Kelly Floyd** (account owner in CRM) by 02:30 CT.
- **Notify Marcus Adeyemi** (Director of Customer Support) by 04:00 CT. Half the restoration target (2 hours) had passed before the 05:05 restoration, which triggers this step.
- **No notice to the VP Sales or Chief Revenue Officer is needed.** Service was restored before the full 4 hours (06:00), and the account is Standard, not Strategic.
- **Claim decision:** Marcus Adeyemi must send a written decision declining the claim, with the reason, by 2026-08-13. That is the 30th day after the claim was received.
- **No credit memo, and no root-cause finding**, are due.

**What the customer must do.** Both of its obligations were met:
- **Report by phone.** The ticket was opened by phone to the hotline, as Severity 1 requires.
- **Claim in writing, on time.** The emailed claim named the ticket and arrived within the window.

The customer still has a standing duty to provide information and access, and to keep a technical contact reachable by phone until restoration. The record shows nothing against that.
